capabilities: Create chess puzzles with Markdown code blocks using fen and bestLine fields
Review puzzles with a spaced repetition system using Again/Hard/Good/Easy ratings
Organize puzzles into decks declared with a #chess-puzzles frontmatter tag
Review a single puzzle, a single deck, pending puzzles only, or all puzzles in the vault
Move puzzles between vaults with review history stored inside the Markdown block
extras: The manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.
motivation: The README says that instead of relying only on public puzzle databases, the plugin encourages players to build a personal collection of patterns from their own games, opening preparation, tactical mistakes, endgame studies and memorable positions.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to practice chess positions or schedule their review, so players depend on public puzzle databases instead of building their own pattern collection.
summary: Chess puzzle trainer that lets players write puzzles as Markdown code blocks and review them with a spaced repetition system.
